## Context
One tool, on its own ticket, because it is the single most likely tool in the server to blow a client's context window. This closes M3 at 20 tools.

Read, in this order, and read nothing else — context exhaustion followed by
invention is the failure mode this spec is shaped to prevent:

1. `SPEC.md` sections 3, 7.3, 7.5, 7.6, 12
2. `neuvector-mcp-spec/phases/PHASE-3-vulnerability.md`
3. `neuvector-mcp-spec/tools/PART-A-inventory-vulnerability-compliance.md` — section **A.0** and the `nv_get_scan_report` entry of the **`Toolset vulnerability`** section
4. `neuvector-mcp-spec/appendix/B-schema-reference.md` for every field you touch
5. `neuvector-mcp-spec/appendix/D-api-conventions.md` sections D.7 and D.8

## Dependencies
- T-008 (must be closed first)

## Files
Create:
- `tests/fixtures/scan_report.json`
Modify:
- `src/neuvector_mcp/models.py`
- `src/neuvector_mcp/tools/vulnerability.py`
- `tests/test_vulnerability.py`
Do NOT touch anything else.

## Steps
1. Append the new output models to the end of `models.py`, in the order the Part file lists them. Nothing above them changes.
2. Write the fixtures named above. Every field name comes from `neuvector-mcp-spec/appendix/B-schema-reference.md` — do not invent one. Every list fixture must hold more items than the smallest `limit` its test uses, so the over-fetch-by-one truncation path is actually exercised.
3. Extend `src/neuvector_mcp/tools/vulnerability.py` with these tools, each one exactly as the Part file specifies its arguments, query mapping, verbatim docstring, output model `from_api()` and envelope key:
   - `nv_get_scan_report` — `GET /v1/scan/image/{id}, GET /v1/scan/workload/{id}, GET /v1/scan/host/{id}, GET /v1/scan/registry/{name}/image/{id}`
4. Extend `tests/test_vulnerability.py` with the test functions the Part file names per tool. Gate rule R8 matches the literal quoted tool name, so every tool name added here must appear as `"nv_..."` inside a test file. Coverage gates at 85% branch, so tests and tools must land in the same commit.
5. Run the gate and report the exact tool count from `make spec`.

## The hard part
A scan report on a large base image carries thousands of CVE entries and the controller does **not** paginate inside a report (D.8). Implement all four parts of the mechanism Part A prescribes:

1. a summary-counts-only mode that returns severity totals and no entries;
2. severity filtering applied **client-side**, after the fetch;
3. a `max_vulnerabilities` cap applied **after** sorting by severity, so the most serious findings survive truncation;
4. `truncated=True` plus a hint naming what was dropped and how to narrow.

A report tool that returns every entry unfiltered is a defect even when its test passes.

One tool over four endpoints, discriminated by `target`. Validate the argument combination locally **before any call**: `target="registry_image"` requires `registry_name`, the others require only `target_id`. Raise `ValidationError_` naming the missing argument. Use `settings.long_request_timeout_s` for the fetch (D.7).

Required tests: `test_get_scan_report_summary_only_omits_entries`, `test_get_scan_report_severity_filter_applied_client_side`, `test_get_scan_report_cap_keeps_highest_severity_first`, `test_get_scan_report_registry_target_requires_registry_name`. Build `scan_report.json` with at least 12 vulnerability entries spanning Critical/High/Medium/Low so the cap and the sort are actually exercised.

## Acceptance
Runnable checks. The task is done only when all pass.
- [ ] `make verify PY=.venv/bin/python`
- [ ] `make spec PY=.venv/bin/python | grep -q "20 tools introspected"`

## Out of scope / guardrails
- Do not read any other PHASE-*.md file. Do not start the next ticket.
- Do not refactor, reformat or 'improve' any module that already passes the gate — every rewrite of passing code is a new chance to break it.
- Do not invent an endpoint, a JSON tag or a field name. If it is not in the appendices, stop and report BLOCKED with the exact thing you could not find.
- Do not edit `scripts/verify_spec.py`, `spec_endpoints.json`, `pyproject.toml` or anything under `neuvector-mcp-spec/`.
- `models.py` is append-only — add new classes at the end in the order the Part file lists them; never redefine `Page`, `WorkloadBrief`, `SystemSummary`, `WriteOutcome`, `PolicyMode`, `Severity` or `_BASE`.
- Every list tool uses the over-fetch-by-one truncation pattern from SPEC.md 7.3. A list tool without it is a defect even if its tests pass.

## Definition of done
`make verify` exits 0, the tool count is exactly as stated, the change is limited
to the files listed above, and the commit is `[T-009] <title>` closing this issue.

content.text:
Done. `github.com/darthzen/neuvector-mcp` is live with a 34-issue queue.

## What's there

**Repo** — public, spec package committed, `agent-build-tools` as a submodule at `build-plan/tools`, config at `build-plan/config.yaml` (repo slug, `build_through: M11`, milestones-only, `entire:` re-anchoring enabled since you'd already run `entire enable`).

**12 milestones** M0–M11, one per spec phase. **34 tickets**, issues #1–#34, all round-tripped back through the toolkit's own parser — deps, file lists and acceptance commands all parse.

The chunking unit is a *coherent tool group*, not a phase, because `verify_spec` R8 fails any tool with no test and coverage gates at 85% — so models + fixtures + tool + tests have to land in one commit. Every ticket gates on:

```
make verify PY=.venv/bin/python
make spec  PY=.venv/bin/python | grep -q "N tools introspected"
```

with N walking 5 → 9 → 13 → 16 → 19 → 20 → … → 72, so a miscount fails the build rather than being reported as "looks right". T-030 additionally gates the 41-tool read-only surface. Each body carries the exact reading list (`§`-cited so `show` injects the SPEC sections automatically), the named test functions, the endpoint/envelope traps (`summarys`, `process_profile_config`, the per-event-kind filter tags, `PATCH /v1/admission/rule` having no `{id}`), and BLOCKED-not-invent guardrails.

The three highest-blast-radius tools each got their own ticket: `nv_get_scan_report` (#9), `nv_apply_network_rule_changes` (#18), `nv_set_admission_state` (#21).

## Running it

```bash
cd ~/Developer/neuvector-mcp
python3 build-plan/tools/agent-tools.py next     # → T-001
python3 build-plan/tools/agent-tools.py show T-001   # body + files + cited SPEC §§
# delegate the code to qwen3-coder:30b via ollama-code
python3 build-plan/tools/agent-tools.py finish T-001 # verify, branch, PR, squash-merge, close
```

`ollama_status` confirms the GPU box at `192.168.7.160:9401` is up with `qwen3-coder:30b` — the model this spec was written for.

## Two things to know

**The queue is serial by design.** Every ticket appends to `models.py`, its toolset module and `server.py`, so the worktree/`batch`/`land` parallel flow won't help here — `capacity` would hand you file-conflicting work. Use `next` → `finish`.

**Python risk at T-001.** `pyenv` only offers 3.11.9 (below the `requires-python = ">=3.12"` floor) and 3.14.5, so the venv will be built on 3.14 against pins written for 3.12/3.13 — `fastmcp==3.4.5`, `pydantic==2.13.4`, `mypy==1.18.2`. The ticket forbids bumping those pins and tells the agent to report BLOCKED with the pip output instead, so if a wheel is missing you'll get a clean stop rather than a silent dependency drift. Installing a 3.13 via pyenv first would sidestep it.

M11 has two `human` tickets — #32 (cluster dry-run, needs secrets) and #33 (live smoke test, needs a controller). The toolkit never picks those up; #34 depends on #31 rather than on them, so the agent queue runs uninterrupted to the end.
